title: Sharvari paired her zardozi-embroidered Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla anarkali with statement chaandbalis

 Open Navigation Menu Menu Trends Sharvari paired her zardozi-embroidered Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla anarkali with statement chaandbalis
 The actor’s floor-sweeping look features a craft form that is among the label's signature techniques By Nupur Sarvaiya 13 November 2026 Instagram.com/sharvari Sharvari has become an unexpected champion of silk tissue fabric. Of late, the actor has been wearing the lustrous textile with a lot of conviction, and her latest outings are testimonies. During the press tour for her upcoming film Yeh Prem Mol Liya , she stepped out in two consecutive looks. The ensemble that stood out was a pistachio green anarkali by Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla .
 Sharvari’s anarkali is part of Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla’s Thousand and One Nights collection. “The set is crafted using tissue and adorned with zardozi hand-embroidery. It is inspired by the timeless allure of old-world aesthetics,” shares Abu Jani. The anarkali features a deep, U-shaped neckline on the fitted yoke at the front and a deep, scooped neckline at the back, which injects a sensual detail into the otherwise conventional silhouette. Intricate embroidery traces the neckline, while the fitted sleeves are finished with heavily embellished cuffs. The bodice opens into a myriad voluminous kalis, embroidered with an ornate zardozi border at the hem. A matching tissue dupatta, generously hand-worked with a decorative kiran border, completed the ensemble.
 Instagram.com/sharvari Zardozi is among the crafts that have become AJSK’s signature techniques. The designer duo has been working with it for over three decades. “What makes zardozi special is the effort it takes to achieve its elegance,” says Sandeep Khosla. “Its maximalism relies entirely on mastery.” This time- and labour-intensive technique traditionally employs metallic threads, often gold and silver, alongside beads, sequins and other embellishments. The veteran couturiers have consistently reimagined this heritage art form across fabrics and silhouettes. Sharvari’s anarkali is just one among many such designs. “It’s one of the most ornamental forms of couture. When embroidered in dense patterns, it can make a garment extremely heavy. A lot heavier than it looks!” add Jani and Khosla.
 Instagram.com/sharvari The actor’s choice of accessories let the embroidery hoard the spotlight. She eschewed the necklace and chose statement chandbali earrings with kaan chains from Surmeyi. Her hair was styled in a half-up, half-down fashion, while her makeup featured flushed cheeks, kohled eyes, bronzy eyeshadow, and a muted nude lip.
 An anarkali, as this Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla set, underscores the importance of investing in textile heritage and time-honoured embroideries. A well-crafted tissue anarkali , with its timeless silhouette and hand-embroidered detailing, is a seasonless garment worthy of being revisited, restyled and repeated for years. Whether worn to a wedding, a festive celebration or a formal family gathering, it can also eventually find its way into the next generation’s wardrobe.
